name: Dirty Pink
lede: Dirty Pink is a muted, slightly brownish rose first recorded by the 2010 xkcd color survey, where volunteers typed names at swatches on screen.

sections.title: A crowd name for a grayed pink
sections.body:
Dirty Pink has no listing in Ridgway, Maerz and Paul, or the ISCC-NBS charts; the only source on file is the xkcd color survey of 2010, where thousands of web users typed names at swatches and this one stuck [1]. The name follows a plain modifier grammar, *dirty* plus [[pink]], the same pattern behind [[dirty-purple|Dirty Purple]] and [[dirty-yellow|Dirty Yellow]]: a base hue read as soiled or faded [1]. At hex #CA7B80 it measures lightness 60 and chroma 33 in LCH, and the nearest ISCC-NBS block reads as a dark pink [1].

Its closest named neighbors are [[old-rose|Old Rose]], 2.9 units off and duller, and [[dusty-rose|Dusty Rose]], 3.0 units off and almost the same; [[antique-pink|Antique Pink]] sits 3.0 units away and more vivid, and [[dusky-pink|Dusky Pink]] 4.1 units away and redder [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pink in 20 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.08 percent, as photographed, rarer than most named colors here [3]. The earliest match is a 1400 painting of a bishop saint, 610 years before the 2010 survey fixed the name, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 6 of 1,674 paintings, 4.3 times the archive's overall rate, after Henri Matisse used it in nudes painted in 1908 and 1909 [3]. These are screen matches on photographs of varnished paintings, not a record of any pigment [3].
